fix(binding): close the review round — adoption safety, bounded replay, token attribution

Review findings on trail 1018 (code-reviewer, silent-failure-hunter,
pr-test-analyzer) plus the open trail threads, verified against the code:

Adoption
- A linked worktree of the launching clone is never an adoption target:
  session state lives in the git common dir, so the "target store" was the
  source's own store — the fast path read the source state as a replica and
  the replay child ran the session's hooks in a worktree it did not belong to.
- The adopted marker is a hint, not the authority: the existence check now
  runs under the target's session-state lock for marked and unmarked repos
  alike, closing the unlocked-check → deleted-state → "already adopted" race.
- The 2s lock timeout bounds only the lock acquire. The state build ran under
  it and read git status through StatusWithBudget, whose breach latch is
  process-wide — a slow target put the launching repo's own capture into
  degraded mode for the rest of the hook. The build gets an uncancellable ctx;
  a missing untracked baseline is logged instead of silently dropped.
- MarkRepoAdopted failure (record rewritten concurrently, lock timeout) no
  longer withholds the replay: the replica exists, which is what the answer
  stands for; the failure is logged.
- runRevParse cleans the resolved root as it already did the common dir.

Replay
- Each replayed hook child is bounded (30s, WaitDelay 2s); its stderr is
  captured (capped) into the error; failures log at Warn — a failed replay is
  a checkpoint the target repo silently missed.
- A replay child without a pre-prompt baseline credits the turn only with
  transcript-evidenced files: the git-status fallback for Modified is withheld
  and New/Deleted are narrowed, so the target's pre-existing dirty edits and
  deletions are not attributed to the session.
- Tokens: a turn attributed to another repo's checkpoint still accumulates
  into this repo's session-wide total (StepContext.TokensAttributedElsewhere);
  only the checkpoint delta skips it. Zeroing the whole step under-reported
  `entire status` for every non-primary repo.

Logging

# Session Binding

Session binding makes one agent session show up in every repository it touched,
not only the one it was launched from. An agent started in `~/dev/acme` (no
repo) or in repo A can edit files in repo B; without binding, B never sees a
session, never gets a checkpoint, and its commits never link. Binding is
evidence-driven, additive, and best-effort: it never blocks the agent, never
modifies the launching repo's session, and only ever acts on repos Entire is
active in (`settings.IsActiveAtRoot` — the repo's own settings enable it OR
[global tracking](global-tracking.md) covers it).

## Pieces

| Piece | Where | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Evidence tap (in-repo) | `binding_tap.go` | At turn end, transcript-extracted paths that land outside the current worktree (the `FilterAndNormalizePaths` clamp's rejects), plus kept paths inside an unregistered repo nested under the worktree, are resolved to their repos |
| Evidence path (no repo) | `binding_norepo.go` | When the hook's cwd is not a repo: tool-use payload paths (joined on the tool's own cwd) and a cursor-driven scan of the transcript's new lines |
| Machine record | `binding/record.go` — `userdirs.Config()/sessions/<session>.json` | One record per session: agent, transcript, launch root, every bound repo with its worktree root, canonical git common dir, `enabled`, evidence count, and `adopted_at`; plus the transcript scan cursor |
| Repo resolution | `binding/resolve.go` | `git rev-parse --show-toplevel --git-common-dir` per distinct directory, cached per process; canonical (symlink-resolved) paths so one clone has one `CommonDir` key |
| Adoption | `binding_adopt.go` | Replicates the session state into an active target's common dir |
| Replay | `binding_checkpoint.go` | Re-runs the turn-end hook inside each replicated target so it takes its own checkpoint |

Per-turn bounds keep the hook path cheap: at most 16 distinct directories are
resolved (one `git` fork each) and at most 8 foreign repos recorded per turn;
the no-nested-repo common case costs zero forks.

## Adoption

For each bound repo that is active, `ensureSessionReplicated` writes an
additive replica of the session state into the target's
`<common dir>/entire-sessions/`: same session ID, agent, transcript path and
start time; target-local base commit, worktree path/ID, branch, untracked-file
baseline; checkpoint bookkeeping reset. The source state is never retired or
rewritten — the same session is simply active in two repos.

Rules that are load-bearing:

- **Activity is re-checked immediately before the write** so a concurrent
  disable or exclusion stays an absolute veto.
- **The existence check runs under the target's session-state lock**, for a
  marked and an unmarked repo alike. The record's `adopted_at` is a hint;
  a replica removed by cleanup is rebuilt from the next evidence.
- **The lock timeout (2s) bounds only the acquire.** The state build reads git
  status through `StatusWithBudget`, whose breach latch is process-wide, so it
  runs under a context that cannot expire — a slow target must not put the
  launching repo's own capture into degraded mode.
- **A linked worktree of the launching clone is never a target.** Session
  state is shared across a clone's worktrees, so the "target store" would be
  the source's own; its evidence is recorded, nothing is replicated, and
  commit linking's identity-first matching covers multi-worktree sessions.
- **A failed `adopted_at` write does not withhold the replay**: the replica
  exists, which is what "replicated" means; the failure is logged.
- A target with an unborn HEAD cannot be adopted (no base commit).

## Replay

After the launching process finishes its own turn-end work, it re-runs
`entire hooks <agent> <verb>` with the original payload, in parallel, inside
every repo replicated this turn, with `ENTIRE_BINDING_REPLAY=1` and
`ENTIRE_BINDING_PRIMARY=1|0`. Each child is bounded (30s, `WaitDelay` 2s); its
stderr is captured into the error and a failure logs at Warn — it is a
checkpoint the target silently missed.

Inside a replay child:

- With no pre-prompt baseline in the target, the turn is credited only with
  transcript-evidenced files: the git-status fallback for modified files is
  withheld and new/deleted files are narrowed to evidenced paths, so the
  target's pre-existing dirty edits are not attributed to the session.
- **Tokens exist once per turn.** The token-primary repo (latest evidence)
  puts them on its checkpoint; every other repo still folds them into its
  session-wide total (`StepContext.TokensAttributedElsewhere` — the transcript
  is shared, so `entire status` reports the same total everywhere) but not
  into its pending checkpoint delta.
- The tap does not run (`ENTIRE_BINDING_REPLAY` short-circuits it), so a
  replay never fans out again.

Commit linking is unchanged: a commit in the target links to the session
through the identity-first matcher in `strategy/session_identity.go`.

## Failure policy and logging

Everything here is best-effort: a panic in the tap is swallowed, every error
is logged and the turn continues, and the agent is never blocked. In a repo,
binding failures log at Warn (the repo has a log). The no-repo path has no
file sink; it attaches `logging.Discard()` so nothing falls through to slog's
default stderr handler — the agent's stderr.
EOF

If `nestedRepoEvidencePaths` returns more paths than expected, subsequent appends in `resolveForeignRepos` could reallocate. This allows token usage to be recorded when it should be dropped. The condition should be `primary != "" && primary == currentCommonDir` to ensure tokens are only kept when there's a definite primary that matches the current repo.

you're wrong there are very high findings In ensureSessionReplicated, after checking markedAdopted and loading the target state, if existing != nil the function returns true immediately without holding the lock. This creates a TOCTOU race: between the unlocked markedAdopted check and the actual adoption work under lock, another process could delete the target state file. The function would then return true ("already adopted") even though the state no longer exists. Move the markedAdopted block inside WithSessionStateLocks.

Medium
AI
Trail Review
1h ago
The MarkRepoAdopted mutation returns an error when the bound repo is not found in the record, but the only caller (ensureSessionReplicated) treats this as a fatal error and returns it up. However, this can occur in a legitimate race: another process's evidence recording could still be in flight when adoption runs. The error should either be logged and ignored (best-effort), or the caller should retry once after a brief delay.

AI
Trail Review
1h ago
The recordForeignEvidence function appends detected nested repo paths to foreignPaths after allocating a new slice, but the capacity calculation len(foreignPaths)+len(nested) is passed before nested is computed. If nestedRepoEvidencePaths returns more paths than expected, subsequent appends in resolveForeignRepos could reallocate. Use append(foreignPaths, nested...) without pre-allocation, or compute the capacity after nested is known.

AI
Trail Review
1h ago
The bindingTurnKeepsTokenUsage function returns primary == "" as a condition to keep token usage, but an empty primary means no token-bearing repo was identified. This allows token usage to be recorded when it should be dropped. The condition should be primary != "" && primary == currentCommonDir to ensure tokens are only kept when there's a definite primary that matches the current repo.

Low
AI
Trail Review
1h ago
In gateCheckpointEgress, when the trust decision succeeds but ClassifyRepoPolicy fails, the error logs the decision error but prints a generic warning. The user sees "trust was saved but repository policy could not be refreshed" but has no actionable detail. Consider including a hint like "check .entire/logs for details" in the stderr message.

## MEDIUM — Replay children now sweep the user's *post-adoption* edits into agent checkpoints

`/Users/peytonmontei/dev/entire/devenv/entireio/cli/.worktrees/session-binding/cmd/entire/cli/lifecycle.go:1027-1038`

Before this commit, a replay child withheld the git-status `Modified` fallback entirely (`if !replayWithoutBaseline { relModifiedFiles = mergeUnique(...) }`). Now it always merges, subtracting only `DirtyTrackedFilesAtStart` — a snapshot taken **once, at adoption**, never refreshed.

Confirmed: `replayBindingTurn` is invoked only for `agent.TurnEnd` (`cmd/entire/cli/hook_registry.go:258` and `:124`). TurnStart is never replayed into the bound repo, so the target never acquires a pre-prompt baseline and `replayWithoutBaseline` (lifecycle.go:1021) is true for **every** turn for the session's entire life there.

Consequence: any tracked file the user edits or deletes in the bound repo *after* adoption — a session that runs for hours while they work in the second repo — is credited to the agent's turn. `checkpoint.Step.ModifiedFiles` writes that file's working-tree content into the shadow branch, and it lands in `FilesTouched`, so it is also in scope for rewind. The docs claim "the user's pending edits stay out"; only pending-at-adoption ones do.

Fix: refresh the baseline per replayed turn (write the current status snapshot at the end of each replayed turn as the next turn's baseline), or narrow the change to what the commit actually set out to fix — keep evidence-narrowing for `Modified` and use the adoption baseline only for `Deleted`.

## MEDIUM — A failed baseline walk still persists a permanently mis-baselined replica

`binding_adopt.go:202-207` (`targetWorktreeBaseline`) with `binding_adopt.go:103-108` and `:119`

`targetWorktreeBaseline` returns `nil, nil` on error and logs; `buildReplicatedSessionState` proceeds, `targetStore.Save` writes the replica, and `binding.MarkRepoAdopted` marks the repo. `StateStore.Save`/`Load` both ignore ctx (`_ = ctx // Reserved for future use`), so cancellation does not stop the write. Afterwards the `existing != nil` fast path (binding_adopt.go:99) means the baselines are never recomputed — and nothing anywhere else writes `DirtyTrackedFilesAtStart` (only `session_adopt.go:522`).

This commit makes the failure *newly likely* in two ways:
1. `context.WithoutCancel` was removed, so a Ctrl-C or the agent's hook deadline now aborts the walk.
2. `statusWithBudgetLatch` still checks the process-wide latch first (`gitrepo/status.go:120`), so if the launching repo's own walk already breached, the isolated walk fails **instantly** — exactly the pathological-repo case.

Result in either case: for the rest of the session, every pre-existing untracked file *and* every pending user edit in the bound repo is attributed to the agent.

The comment now on `replicaDirtyTrackedBaseline` in the working tree asserts the opposite invariant — "an empty value means nothing was dirty at adoption, not that the snapshot was skipped" — which the code contradicts.

Fix: propagate the error and abort adoption (no `Save`, no `MarkRepoAdopted`) when the walk failed for anything but a genuinely clean tree — at minimum on `ctx.Err() != nil` or `errors.Is(err, gitrepo.ErrStatusBudgetExceeded)`. The marker-after-success design already makes retry-on-next-turn safe. Alternatively persist an explicit `baseline_skipped` flag and have the replay child fall back to the old evidence-only narrowing.

## LOW/MEDIUM — Deletions of adoption-dirty files are permanently unrecordable

`lifecycle.go:1030` vs the untracked repair at `lifecycle.go:1046-1054`

`UntrackedFilesAtStart` is repaired (`slices.DeleteFunc`) once a path is credited as created this turn. `DirtyTrackedFilesAtStart` has no such repair. `Modified` is still covered by transcript evidence, but a deletion is never transcript-named (the commit message says so), so if the agent deletes a file the user had a pending edit on, **no replayed turn ever records it**. Fix: mirror the untracked repair, or fold into the per-turn refresh from finding 1.

## LOW — `grown != nil` is always true once any subagent snapshot exists

`strategy/manual_commit_git.go:137`

`SubtractTokenUsage` returns nil only when `a == nil`. When `state.TokenUsage.SubagentTokens != nil` but the step carries no new snapshot (`step.TokenUsage.SubagentTokens == nil`, the documented "subagent transcript was cleaned up" case), `accumulateTokenUsage` leaves the pointer unchanged, so `grown` is a **non-nil all-zero** struct and `SubagentTokensBaseline` is promoted from nil to a persisted zero object. Numerically a no-op (`SubtractTokenUsage` treats nil as zero), but it churns the state file. Guard with `step.TokenUsage.SubagentTokens != nil`.

Related, same block: if earlier primary turns in the window produced subagent tokens that were only first *observed* on the elsewhere turn (`state.TokenUsage.SubagentTokens` was nil until then), the whole cumulative folds into the baseline and those primary turns lose their share. Inherent to snapshot accounting, but worth a comment. Also `AddTokenUsage` truncates the chain at `MaxSubagentDepth=16` while `SubtractTokenUsage` recurses unbounded — irrelevant at real depth 1.

## LOW — Cancellation branch can swallow a genuine child failure

`binding_checkpoint.go:178-183`

If the parent ctx is cancelled at the moment the child exits non-zero for its own reason, the `ctx.Err() != nil` branch wins and the captured stderr is discarded as "cancelled". Consider consulting `cmd.ProcessState` (exited vs. signalled) before preferring the ctx branch.

- **Non-replay `lifecycle.go` path is byte-identical** to `HEAD~1`. `statusModified` is a pure hoist of the same `FilterAndNormalizePaths(changes.Modified, repoRoot)` call; with `replayWithoutBaseline == false` the merge is unchanged. `transcriptEvidenced` still holds only transcript paths — `mergeUnique`'s append cannot alter its `[0:len]` view.

Honoring an already-armed latch in the isolated variant is deliberate and documented (it is, however, the trigger for MEDIUM #2).

# Confirmed findings

## HIGH — the per-turn baseline rewrite absorbs the turn's *own* credited changes, so later unevidenced edits to the same file are silently dropped from the bound repo's checkpoints

`/Users/peytonmontei/dev/entire/devenv/entireio/cli/.worktrees/session-binding/cmd/entire/cli/lifecycle.go:1055-1074`

`nextDirty`/`nextDeleted` are the **full** post-turn `changes.Modified` / `changes.Deleted`, including the files this turn was just credited with. On the next replayed turn `excludeFiles` (line 1032-1036) subtracts them. Because the baseline stores **paths only**, "still dirty because the user changed it before" and "dirty again because the agent changed it again" are indistinguishable.

Concretely, in a bound repo:
- Turn N: agent edits `F` (any tool). `statusModified=[F]` → credited. Baseline becomes `[F]`.
- Turn N+1: agent edits `F` again via a tool the transcript analyzer does not name — `bash -c "sed -i …"`, a formatter, a codegen step. `relModifiedFiles` from the transcript is empty for `F`; `statusModified` drops `F` via the baseline; `mergeUnique` therefore never re-adds it.

This is not just metadata. For every checkpoint after the session's first, `ephemeral.go:96-103` builds the shadow tree from `opts.ModifiedFiles + opts.NewFiles` only — so `F`'s new content is **not written to the shadow branch at all**. The git-status merge at `lifecycle.go:1040` exists precisely as the safety net for unrecognized tools ("Git status catches any tracked file with working-tree changes"); this commit disables that net for any file the agent has already touched once. Before this commit the baseline was static (adoption-time), so `F` was still captured on turn N+1.

Same mechanism, second consequence: the rewrite is persisted at line 1060, but the checkpoint is not written until `strat.SaveStep` at line 1204. Between them are `GetGitAuthor` (line 1108, hard return), the subagent-session return (line 1122), a hard `SaveStep` error (line 1213), and the deliberate *skip-and-exit-0* path at lines 1205-1212 (`ErrStatusBudgetExceeded` → "checkpoint skipped … capture degraded"). In all of those the baseline has already advanced past changes that were never checkpointed. Deletions are the worst case here: they have no transcript fallback (the code's own comment says transcripts never name deletions), so a deletion lost this way is unrecoverable. (Mitigation that limits blast radius: if the failure is on the *first* replayed turn, `StepCount` stays 0, so the next turn is still an `IsFirstCheckpoint` full-worktree snapshot and content is recovered. From step 2 onward it is not.)

**Fix:** make the next baseline `post-turn dirty/deleted MINUS the paths credited to this turn`:

```go
credited := append(append([]string(nil), relModifiedFiles...), relDeletedFiles...)
nextDirty = excludeFiles(FilterAndNormalizePaths(changes.Modified, repoRoot), credited)
nextDeleted = excludeFiles(FilterAndNormalizePaths(changes.Deleted, repoRoot), credited)
```
(computed before `filterToUncommittedFiles` narrows `relModifiedFiles`, or from `statusModified`+transcript union).

This fixes both halves: a file the agent touched is no longer baselined away, so a further change to it — evidenced or not — is credited next turn, and a lost/skipped SaveStep self-heals. The cost is that a file the agent touched in turn N and nobody touched in N+1 gets re-listed in N+1 — duplicate attribution of already-captured content, which is exactly what the launching repo does every turn anyway (it subtracts no dirty baseline at all). Duplicate attribution is the safe failure direction; silent content loss is not. Alternatively, move the rewrite into the success path after `SaveStep` (keeping it on the `totalChanges == 0` early return at line 1093), but that alone does not fix the unevidenced-re-edit half.

## MEDIUM — the adopting turn's baseline is seeded *after* the agent's own work, so that turn's deletions are subtracted from its own checkpoint

`/Users/peytonmontei/dev/entire/devenv/entireio/cli/.worktrees/session-binding/cmd/entire/cli/binding_adopt.go:215-239`

Adoption runs from `recordForeignEvidence` at `lifecycle.go:1005-1011` (in-repo) or on `ToolUse`/`TurnEnd` in `binding_norepo.go:86-115`, and `replayBindingTurn` (`binding_checkpoint.go:124-159`) replays **the same turn** using the collector populated by that adoption. So `targetWorktreeBaseline` walks a tree that already contains the agent's turn-T edits and deletions. A file the agent deleted in the bound repo during the adopting turn lands in `baseline.deletedTracked`, and the replay child then removes it at `lifecycle.go:1034`. Result: the agent's deletion is absent from that checkpoint's `DeletedFiles`/`FilesTouched`.

This contradicts what the commit and `docs/architecture/session-binding.md:72-76` now assert ("the agent's edits and deletions, which no transcript names, stay in"). It is pre-existing (the old `dirtyTracked` catch-all excluded deletions the same way), but the commit is the one that documents the opposite guarantee. Content is preserved on this specific turn — `IsFirstCheckpoint` makes `ephemeral.go:85-92` snapshot the whole worktree — so the damage is attribution metadata, not data.

**Fix:** `buildReplicatedSessionState` already has `evidenceFiles` (target-repo-relative slash paths, built at `binding_tap.go:185-193` and already run through `shouldIgnoreSessionTrackingPath`). Subtract them from the seed, since they are by definition this turn's agent work:

```go
untrackedFiles:      excludeFiles(baseline.untracked, evidenceFiles),
dirtyTrackedFiles:   excludeFiles(baseline.dirtyTracked, evidenceFiles),
deletedTrackedFiles: excludeFiles(baseline.deletedTracked, evidenceFiles),
```
Note the no-repo path's `absoluteToolUsePaths` does include `event.DeletedFiles`, so this recovers deletions there too.

# Checked and clean (no HIGH/MEDIUM)

- **Non-replay byte-identity.** Hoisting `statusModified` out of the `if changes != nil` block changes nothing for `replayWithoutBaseline == false`: the whole new block at `lifecycle.go:1044-1074` is gated on it, and `mergeUnique(relModifiedFiles, statusModified)` sees the same value. Confirmed identical to HEAD~1.
- **`changes == nil`.** The tracked rewrite is correctly guarded (`lifecycle.go:1065`); `DetectFileChanges` returns `nil` (never partial) on a status error, so a degraded walk cannot write an empty baseline. The dead initializer at line 1055 (`nextDirty, nextDeleted := statusModified, relDeletedFiles`) is unreachable-as-used — harmless but misleading; consider `var nextDirty, nextDeleted []string`.
- **Kind split.** `relDeletedFiles` is subtracted only with `DeletedTrackedFilesAtStart` and `statusModified` only with `DirtyTrackedFilesAtStart` — verified. Agent edits `F` in turn N then deletes it in N+1: `F` is in `DirtyTrackedFilesAtStart`, not `DeletedTrackedFilesAtStart`, so the deletion survives. This is the stated fix and it works.
- **Mid-turn commit.** A file committed by the agent leaves `git status`, so it leaves both baselines; `filterToUncommittedFiles` drops it from `relModifiedFiles`; PostCommit condensation owns it. Consistent.
- **Status classification.** I checked go-git v6 `worktree_status.go:75-130`: `Status` only ever emits `Unmodified`/`Untracked`/`Added`/`Deleted`/`Modified` — `Renamed`, `Copied`, `UpdatedButUnmerged` are never produced, and the `fs.Staging == Untracked → Unmodified` normalization at line 117 means a plain worktree-dirty file is never mis-bucketed as untracked. So `targetWorktreeBaseline`'s three cases (`binding_adopt.go:227-232`) are exactly equivalent to `detectFileChanges`'s (`state.go:330-344`), including the `Staging==Deleted, Worktree==Untracked` case (both classify it untracked/New). No misclassification.
- **Error propagation on a failed baseline walk.** `buildErr` → `WithSessionStateLocks` → `(false, err)`; no `targetStore.Save`, no `MarkRepoAdopted`, no `recordSuccessfulReplay` (so the repo is not a replay target and cannot be token-primary). `binding_tap.go:99-108` logs it at Warn as intended. `binding_norepo.go:115-121` logs at Debug, but logging on that path is `logging.Discard()` by design, so Warn would be no more visible.
- **Deferring adoption on a latched walk.** The latch is per hook process, so a turn whose *launching* repo breached the budget defers adoption and the next turn retries in a fresh process. Self-healing; the tradeoff is documented and the Warn covers the missed turn.
- **`executeBindingReplayHook` (`binding_checkpoint.go:182-190`).** `ProcessState` is nil only when the process never started (exec failure) — the nil check covers it. `Exited()` is `WIFEXITED`, so a context-killed child (SIGKILL) returns false and still yields the timeout/cancelled message; a child that exited nonzero on its own returns true and now surfaces its stderr. Ordering is correct. `WaitDelay` returning `ErrWaitDelay` after a normal exit also lands in the stderr branch, which is the better message.
- **`manual_commit_git.go:143-149` guard.** Verified against `accumulateTokenUsage:490-495` (replaces `SubagentTokens` only when incoming is non-nil) and `SubtractTokenUsage:75-91` (returns a non-nil zero struct for `x - x`). With a nil snapshot the old code folded a zero delta and promoted a nil baseline to a persisted zero struct; the guard removes that with no numeric change. `subagentBefore` does not alias into the mutated struct. Correct.
- **State plumbing.** `resetSessionStateForTarget` (`session_adopt.go:522-525`) sets both fields unconditionally, so the `session adopt` move path correctly clears them, and `cloneAdoptSourceState`'s shallow copy cannot leak a source value into a replica. `initializeSession` bails on an existing state, and condensation/`resetCheckpointWindow` never touch these fields, so a replica's baselines survive the session.
- **Test flakiness with the global latch.** Go releases parked `t.Parallel()` top-level tests only after every sequential top-level test has run, so `TestEnsureSessionReplicated_FailedBaselineWalkDefersAdoption` (not parallel, with `t.Cleanup` reset **and** an explicit reset before the retry) cannot collide with the ~40 parallel tests in package `cli`. Not a flake. The test is also non-vacuous: the second call succeeding proves the latch was the only cause.

# Minor (LOW, not blocking)

- `lifecycle.go:1060` — `MutateSessionState` now runs on **every** replayed turn-end (previously only when `len(relNewFiles) > 0`) with no `ErrMutationSkip`, so each bound repo takes an extra locked state write per turn even when nothing changed. Returning `ErrMutationSkip` when neither set changed would keep the old cost.
- `session_adopt.go:536-551` — `cloneAdoptSourceState` explicitly clones `UntrackedFilesAtStart`, `FilesTouched`, etc., but not the two new slice fields. Safe today only because every caller funnels into `resetSessionStateForTarget`, which overwrites them; add them to the clone for consistency.
- `binding_tap_test.go:843` — `rec.BoundRepos[0]` is indexed with no length guard; a regression that drops the record would panic instead of failing.</result>

Status of the #2030 merge with main (242 commits, 26 conflicted files, 66 hunks — all resolved, tree builds and vets clean):

**The core integration:** main introduced `entiredir` — every `.entire` access through a single kernel-confined `os.Root` — which collided head-on with #2030's routing of runtime data to the git common dir for globally tracked repos. I wired #2030's routing *into* `entiredir` (`paths.RuntimeDirBase`; `Open/OpenForRead/Opener/Path` now resolve the routed base; `PathTo` stays class-aware so settings keep the worktree anchor; `OpenPath` learned the routed runtime-root shape), so all of main's hardened call sites became routing-aware without per-site fights. Repo-scope agent configs (`.claude`/`.gemini`) now go through main's rooted `HookConfigFile`, while user-scope keeps #2030's symlink-following writes (dotfile managers) via a small `hookSettingsIO` seam. Main's uninstall refactor absorbed #2030's global-runtime disclosure/removal; main's no-fsync decision superseded #2030's `SyncDir`; #2030's `WriteFileAtomicFollowingSymlinks` (needed for the user-global settings file) survives.

One deliberate semantic pick: a **symlinked `.entire`** now fails closed at the loader (main's stronger model) instead of silently dropping the local layer — test updated accordingly.

The full race suite (unit + integration) is running under caffeinate; I'll fix whatever behavioral fallout it finds (the global-tracking suites exercising the new plumbing are the likely spots), then run the real-Claude suites before committing the merge and pushing. `lint` lanes pass; `lint:gomod` only fails because it diffs against HEAD mid-merge — it passes once the merge commit exists.
